name: CareTria (2nd Position)
desc:
Pharmacy Patient Advocate | $19 to $24/hr | Inbound and Outbound Patient Enrollment Support, No Sales Expectations
Company: CareTria
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
CareTria runs patient support programs for drug makers. In this role, you help patients enroll in a Patient Assistance Program (PAP), which helps people who can't afford their medication get it from the manufacturer. You'll review enrollment forms, call patients to check that they qualify, and reach out to patients or their doctor's office for any missing information. You'll let patients and providers know about approvals, denials, and next steps, and schedule medication shipments to the patient or their provider. You'll answer inbound calls, make outbound calls, explain the program to patients and office staff, and report any side effects or product complaints that come up. Enrollments have deadlines, so prioritizing your work matters.

Soft Skills
- Empathy and compassion
- Clear explanations of insurance and program rules
- Organization and follow-through
- Prioritizing to meet deadlines
- Tact when sharing a denial
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or equivalent
Required Experience: 2 years in customer service, including 1 year in a call center, plus experience with insurance and benefit investigations and knowledge of U.S. private and government payers (like Medicare and Medicaid)
Preferred Experience: Associate degree or technical training, 2 years in pharmacy, managed care, Medicaid or Medicare, pharma or biotech, insurance, or a medical office, HIPAA and patient services experience, and bilingual English and Spanish

Required Skills:
- Excellent verbal and written communication
- Organized and detail-oriented
- Balancing several priorities and deadlines
- Adaptable when things change
- Basic math and logical thinking
- Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook
- Works well alone and on a team
- Empathy and tact with patients

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has call center experience in insurance, a pharmacy, or a doctor's office
- Has done benefits verification or insurance checks
- Wants to help patients get medication they couldn't otherwise afford
- Speaks Spanish as well as English

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Has no insurance or benefits verification experience
- Has less than 1 year of call center experience
- Finds it hard to tell someone they were denied
- Struggles with deadlines and paperwork
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
5. Complete CareTria's pre-employment screening:
- Work authorization: I-9 and E-Verify
- Education verification with your highest level of school
- 7-year criminal background check (federal and state)
- 7-year employment verification with past employers
- Drug screen at a testing site within 3 days of the offer
Steps 1 to 4 are an estimated process. Step 5 comes directly from CareTria.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Patient assistance programs
- Benefits investigation
- Insurance verification
- Medicare and Medicaid
- Patient enrollment
- Inbound and outbound calls
- Healthcare provider support
- Adverse event reporting
- HIPAA compliance
- Bilingual Spanish

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your call center experience and any work with insurance or benefits.
- What's the difference between private insurance and government payers like Medicare and Medicaid?
- A patient was denied for the program. How would you explain it and share next steps?
- Tell us about a time you had to track down missing information to finish a task. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you managed several deadlines at once. How did you prioritize, and how did it turn out?

Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $19 to $24/hr, with possible performance bonuses for eligible employees.
-Shift: Must have availability for any shift based on business needs. Can be discussed in final interview, offer stage.
-Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement plan options, PTO, paid parental leave, and employee assistance programs.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in the posting. Ask in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: 7-year federal and state criminal background check. Yes, 7 years+, per our current listing.
-Drug Test: Required. Drug screen at a testing site within 3 days of the offer.
-Notes: This is a higher-paying step up from CareTria's Patient Support Representative role, best for a participant with insurance or benefits verification experience. Pre-employment screening includes I-9 and E-Verify, education verification, a 7-year background check, 7-year employment verification, and a drug screen. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Pharmacy Patient Advocate → Senior Patient Advocate → Patient Access or Reimbursement Specialist → Team Lead → Patient Access Supervisor. This role builds insurance, benefits verification, and patient access skills.
